claims.claim: Meridian's watershed has four creeks mapped by FEMA as Special Flood Hazard Areas: Fivemile, Eightmile, Ninemile and Tenmile Creeks. On request, Meridian Public Works will determine whether a property is in or out of a Special Flood Hazard Area or floodway, give base flood elevation data, share any history of flooding at the site, and provide copies of Elevation Certificates for properties permitted through the city.
claims.quotedLanguage: Meridian's watershed consists of four creeks that are mapped by FEMA as Special Flood Hazard Areas: Fivemile, Eightmile, Ninemile, and Tenmile Creeks.

claims.claim: In Meridian, public utility, drainage and irrigation easements are typically 10 feet wide along the street and rear yards and 5 feet along side yards, can be larger depending on purpose, and also carry lot drainage and pressurized irrigation lines; utility providers, including the irrigation districts, can access them. The city lists Nampa & Meridian, Settlers, Boise-Kuna and Pioneer among the irrigation providers operating in Meridian.
claims.quotedLanguage: Public utility, drainage, and irrigation easements are typically 10 feet wide along the required street and rear yards and 5 feet along the side yard

claims.claim: Meridian's City Clerk is the city's custodian of records; permit information for Community Development is searchable online without a user account, a free public user account gives fuller search, and other records go through a public records request.
claims.quotedLanguage: The City Clerk is the City of Meridian's custodian of records and is designated to receive public records requests on behalf of the City of Meridian. ... Simple search capability is available without a user account

claims.claim: The City of Meridian explains that a property inside one of its urban renewal districts shows two line items on its tax bill, for the base and the increment, but that the total charged is the same as for a property in the same taxing districts outside one; districts close within 20 years of creation.
claims.quotedLanguage: Property owners within a district do have two-line items on their tax bill, for the base and the increment, but the total amount charged to an individual taxpayer is the same whether the property is inside or outside an urban renewal district.

claims.claim: Nampa & Meridian Irrigation District bases its assessment on the water right allocated to the land, not on how much water is used, and says the property owner is ultimately responsible for paying it, whether or not a mortgage company pays it; an exclusion is available only for land without access to irrigation water and must be signed by all deeded owners.
claims.quotedLanguage: This assessment is for the water right that has been allocated to your land. It is not based on your usage of the water; it is based on the size of your water right. ... The property owner is ultimately responsible for paying the irrigation tax.
claims.notes: Entity tagged city:meridian because Meridian is the only Ada County city page using it; NMID also serves Nampa (Canyon County).

claims.claim: Nampa & Meridian Irrigation District owns and operates pressurized urban irrigation systems it contracted to build in new subdivisions, maintaining the pump station and main line to the first valve off the main, while homeowners own their own sprinkler systems; land with water rights in another irrigation district as well receives a tax notice from both.
claims.quotedLanguage: The system then becomes the property of the Irrigation District, and the Irrigation District will operate and maintain the system and all the water lines to the delivery valve in the individual lots. ... Your land may have water rights in another Irrigation District, if so, you will receive a tax notice from both

claims.claim: To identify an address's irrigation provider, Nampa & Meridian Irrigation District says to check the bill first, because water can come from an irrigation district or be serviced by a city, then use the Idaho Department of Water Resources' Irrigation Organizations Map, which does not show city-serviced water.
claims.quotedLanguage: your statement shows who is servicing your water. Sometimes your water comes from an irrigation district, but your water can also be serviced from the city.
